title: Explore Vlorë’s Coastal Highway: Best Beaches in Vlore by Car
excerpt: Drive the stunning Vlorë coastal highway from Tirana and discover the four top beaches where the Adriatic meets the Ionian – perfect for a self‑drive day trip.
keywords: best beaches in Vlore by car
intro: Arriving at Tirana Rinas Airport? A short drive north brings you to Vlorë, the gateway where the shallow Adriatic sand meets the rugged Ionian pebble coves. With a rental from AutoConnect, you can cruise the cliff‑side highway at your own pace and hop between the region’s most rewarding beaches.

sections.title: Best Beaches in Vlore by Car: The North‑Adriatic Sand
sections.body: The northern stretch of Vlorë’s coastline offers wide, golden‑sand beaches that are ideal for families and sun‑seekers. Starting with the popular Zvernec Beach, the soft sand extends for several kilometres, giving ample space for beach games and picnics. Because the Adriatic side is flat, parking is easy and the road runs parallel to the shoreline, making it a perfect first stop for anyone exploring the best beaches in Vlore by car.

sections.title: South‑Ionian Pebble Coves: Drymades and Beyond
sections.body: Cross the city centre and the highway bends sharply as you enter the Ionian side, where dramatic cliffs give way to secluded pebble coves. Drymades Beach, just 12 km south of Vlorë, is a highlight – crystal‑clear water, dramatic rock formations and a tranquil vibe. A short detour leads to the hidden gems of Radhimë and Borsh, each reachable only by a narrow road that rewards drivers with breathtaking sea views.

sections.title: Driving Tips for the Coastal Highway
sections.body: The coastal road is scenic but demands attention. Sections are narrow and perched on cliffs, so keep a moderate speed and be ready to pull over at designated spots for oncoming traffic. Fuel stations are sparse between Vlorë and the southern coves, so fill up in town. With a rental from AutoConnect at the airport, you avoid the typical €25 one‑way taxi fare to Drymades and gain the freedom to explore multiple beaches in a single day.

sections.title: Where to Park and Take a Break
sections.body: Most major beaches have small parking lots near the entrance; arrive early in summer to secure a spot. At Zvernec you’ll find shaded benches and a kiosk, while Drymades offers a modest beach bar and clean restrooms. Pack water, sunscreen and a light snack – services are limited on the more remote coves, and a quick stop at a local konoba (tavern) can turn a simple beach day into a memorable culinary experience.

tip.title: Leave Early to Beat the Cliffs
tip.body: Start your drive before 9 am to avoid the midday rush on the narrow cliff sections and to enjoy cooler temperatures for a more comfortable beach hop.

faq.question: Can you easily drive to the beaches south of Vlorë?
faq.answer: Yes – the southern beaches are reachable by the main coastal highway, but the road becomes narrower and more winding, so a confident driver and a rental car are recommended.

faq.question: Are the beaches in Vlorë sandy or pebbly?
faq.answer: The northern Adriatic beaches are primarily sandy, while the southern Ionian coves are mostly pebbly or rocky, offering a contrast that many visitors enjoy.

faq.question: How much does a taxi cost from Vlorë to Drymades beach?
faq.answer: A one‑way taxi ride from Vlorë to Drymades typically costs around €25, making a rental car a more economical choice for multiple beach visits.
